Pharmaceutical company AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV) met Wall Street's revenue expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 10.3% year on year to $17.4 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $3.82 per share was 1.3% above analysts' consensus estimates. Is now the time to buy ABBV? Find out in our full research report (it's free). Revenue $17.4 billion vs S&P analysts' estimates of $17.34 billion (10.3% year-on-year growth, in line) Adjusted EPS $3.82 vs S&P analysts' estimates of $3.77 (1.3% beat) Adjusted EPS guidance Management reiterated its full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $13.97 at the midpoint Operating margin 36%, up from 12.1% in the same quarter last year AbbVie's third quarter was marked by a positive market reaction, attributed to robust sales growth across its immunology and neuroscience portfolios. Management highlighted the continued momentum of key products like SKYRIZI, RINVOQ, and VRAYLAR, each delivering double-digit revenue increases. CEO Rob Michael emphasized that "nine key products delivered double-digit growth," with particular strength in immunology and progress in new indications for neuroscience therapies. The quarter's performance also benefited from newly approved treatments and advancements in product delivery, reflecting strong commercial execution. Looking forward, AbbVie's outlook is shaped by anticipated launches, expanding indications, and ongoing pipeline development. Management expects the recent subcutaneous induction approval for SKYRIZI in Crohn's disease and upcoming launches for RINVOQ in vitiligo and alopecia areata to contribute meaningfully to future growth. CFO Scott Reents indicated that new product launches and continued uptake in neuroscience, including the Parkinson's therapy JUVMO, will help sustain momentum. Management also sees opportunities in advancing combination therapies and new developments in oncology and obesity. Management attributed the quarter's performance to volume gains in immunology and neuroscience, product lifecycle expansion, and execution on new launches. Immunology volume expansion: SKYRIZI and RINVOQ both saw strong growth across indications, with SKYRIZI prescription trends holding up despite new competition. The subcutaneous induction approval in Crohn's disease is expected to further strengthen SKYRIZI's position and accelerate new patient share in coming quarters. Neuroscience product momentum: The company's neuroscience segment was driven by VRAYLAR, UBRELVY, Qulipta, and the recent launch of JUVMO for Parkinson's disease. Management noted that JUVMO, with its differentiated profile, is expected to gradually ramp up as commercial and Medicare coverage expands. Oncology pipeline progress: AbbVie highlighted positive developments in multiple myeloma (etentamig) and large B-cell lymphoma (Epkinly), with regulatory submissions underway and approvals anticipated next year. Management described these assets as underappreciated by the market and important contributors for future revenue. Aesthetics stabilization: While overall aesthetics sales declined slightly, BOTOX Cosmetic revenues grew modestly. Management observed early signs of stabilization in the aesthetics segment and is rolling out Boey, a new fast-acting toxin, in Europe and Canada. Strategic M&A and pipeline investments: The acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics added differentiated assets in dermatology and respiratory diseases, while business development remains focused on augmenting depth in core therapeutic areas rather than pursuing large-scale deals. AbbVie's guidance centers on continued growth in immunology and neuroscience, new indication launches, and execution of its advancing pipeline strategy. New indication launches: Management expects the launch of SKYRIZI subcutaneous induction in Crohn's disease and U.S. launches of RINVOQ in vitiligo and alopecia areata to drive further growth. These new indications are anticipated to expand the addressable patient base and reinforce market share in key therapeutic areas. Pipeline milestones and regulatory events: Anticipated approvals for etentamig in multiple myeloma and Epkinly in large B-cell lymphoma are seen as major near-term catalysts. Additionally, positive interim data from various late-stage trials, particularly in immunology and neuroscience, could accelerate future launches and revenue streams. Market access and payer dynamics: Management identified strong payer access for new launches as a key to sustaining growth, with low single-digit rebate concessions expected. However, external factors such as regulatory changes, competitive pressures, and evolving reimbursement frameworks present ongoing risks. In the coming quarters, the StockStory team will monitor (1) the adoption and uptake of new indications for SKYRIZI and RINVOQ, (2) regulatory progress and potential approvals for key oncology and neuroscience assets, and (3) stabilization trends in the aesthetics portfolio, particularly the rollout of Boey. Additional late-stage clinical trial data and results from combination therapies in immunology will also be important markers of success. title: AbbVie's Humira Era Is Fading, But Its New Growth Engines Face Another Test - MarketBeat
content:
AbbVie completed the Apogee Therapeutics acquisition during the quarter. Apogee Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharma focused on immunological and inflammatory diseases, complementing AbbVie’s core portfolio with several therapies in development. Other growth avenues include the Neurosciences and Oncology segments, which have promising pipelines of their own, in addition to today's drivers. The Neurosciences segment is supported by Vraylar and Botox Therapeutic, along with Ubrelvy and Qulipta. Oncology is also contributing, although growth has been more modest. Looking ahead, the company has approximately one dozen promising therapies in advanced testing across segments, including expanded treatments for Skyrizi and Rinvoq. AbbVie expects those two drugs to generate more than $32 billion in combined sales in 2026. AbbVie reported third-quarter results, with revenue of $17.4 billion, up 10.3% year over year and just above consensus. Sales were driven by a 16.3% increase in Immunology, including solid gains in Skyrizi and Rinvoq, a 19.4% increase in Neurosciences, and a 0.8% increase in Oncology. Aesthetics, including Botox Cosmetic, fell 1.4% but remains a cash driver. Margin news is more impressive, with costs and acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) milestones far less than last year, resulting in wider gross and operating margins. Adjusted operating margin came in at nearly 49%, up almost 18 percentage points, sufficient to drive triple-digit increases in the GAAP and adjusted earnings figures. Adjusted earnings per share of $3.82 grew 105%, outperforming MarketBeat’s consensus by about nine cents and enabling management to raise guidance for the second time this year. The company significantly raised its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) target, setting the low end at $13.95, in line with consensus, and the high at $13.99. ABBV could perform near the high end of its forecast or potentially outperform it, given Q3 strengths and developments, including expanded approvals for key drugs. AbbVie’s investment appeal lies in its growth but centers on profitability, cash flow, and its capacity for capital returns. Share buybacks aren’t the primary driver but help keep the share count steady while dividends are distributed. The current dividend yields approximately 2.41% in early November, more than double the broad market average, with above-average distribution growth also forecasted. AbbVie has a Dividend King-level dividend growth record, including its history with Abbott Laboratories. Analysts' response to Q3 results and guidance included several price target increases. Some analyst targets reach $340 or higher, and MarketBeat tracks 30 analyst ratings. The commentary focuses on execution and the higher guidance, which keeps them bullish. As it stands, the 30 analysts tracked rate the stock as a Moderate Buy with an 80% Buy-side bias and no Sell ratings logged, forecasting a slight correction at the consensus, but the trend matters. Consensus is up versus last year, last quarter, and early October, providing a tailwind. Institutional investors have also been buying ABBV in 2026, with institutional ownership now exceeding 70% of shares. This reflects substantial institutional interest, although it doesn't guarantee support during market pullbacks. ABBV’s biggest risks are upcoming patent cliffs, including one for Skyrizi in 2033. Rinvoq also faces a cliff, but it's been pushed back until much later in the coming decade due to legal settlements. The offset is seven more years of Rinvoq growth and dominance, compounded by a robust pipeline that strengthens quarterly. Humira is no longer a risk. Chart price action is favorable following the release. ABBV shares moved up to a fresh high, breaking out of near-term consolidation. The pattern suggests potential upside of about $30, putting the near-term target near $320, just below the high end of analysts' forecasts. title: AbbVie Stock Hits a Record After a 5.2% Dividend Raise: Why Its 276% Payout Ratio Doesn’t Tell the Entire Story - TIKR.com
content: DCdisplay from Hình ảnh của Tran Helen and SUWANNAR KAWILA via Canva AbbVie (ABBV) gave dividend investors the answer they were waiting for on Friday, October 30. Its third-quarter report showed revenue of $17.404 billion, up 10.3%, and adjusted EPS of $3.82. It also raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95 to $13.99, from $13.76 to $13.96, and lifted the quarterly dividend 5.2% to $1.82 a share, starting with the February 16, 2027 payment. Skyrizi and Rinvoq did the heavy lifting again. Skyrizi sales rose 22.7% to $5.776 billion and Rinvoq rose 23.9% to $2.706 billion, and on the earnings call management lifted their full-year targets to $21.8 billion and $10.3 billion. The stock closed at a record $294.89, up 1.4%. In September, AbbVie stock’s 2.74% yield sat near a two-year low while its payout ratio looked stretched. The open question was simple: could earnings grow fast enough to fund another raise without the payout climbing further? Friday’s numbers say yes. The headline doubling in Q3 adjusted EPS, from $1.86, is mostly a base effect: last year’s quarter carried a $1.50 charge for acquired R&D, against $0.11 this time. Strip that out of both quarters and adjusted EPS still rose about 17%, from $3.36 to $3.93. A 5.2% dividend increase is a small slice of that. On a GAAP basis, AbbVie hasn’t covered its dividend for three straight years. TIKR shows the payout ratio climbing from 216.72% in 2023 to 275.84% in 2025. Those figures are driven by non-cash items. In Q3 alone, intangible amortization and contingent-consideration charges took $1.25 off GAAP EPS, which came in at $2.37. Cash tells a different story: AbbVie generated about $14 billion of free cash flow in the first nine months, roughly 1.5 times the $9.2 billion or so it paid in dividends over the same stretch. Against adjusted earnings, the new $7.28 annual dividend uses about 52% of the guidance midpoint. The Street expects that share to keep falling. Analysts expect normalized EPS of $16.16 in 2027 and $18.00 in 2028, growth of 15.1% and 11.4%. Holding the dividend at $7.28, the payout would drop to about 45% in 2027 and 40% in 2028. Even a few more 5% raises leave room to spare. See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AbbVie, along with Wall Street’s revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AbbVie’s Analyst Ratings The dividend got safer, but buying it got pricier. The stock is up about 12% from the $263 it traded at in September, and the yield has slid with it. The trailing yield now sits at 2.35%, below the 2.65% floor the September piece flagged and well under the 3.12% average on TIKR’s chart. Even on the new $1.82 payment, the forward yield is only about 2.47%. The guidance raise also deserves a closer look. The new range implies fourth-quarter EPS of $3.83 to $3.87, only a few cents above what the old midpoint implied. Most of the $0.11 lift is Q3’s beat carried forward, not a stronger Q4. Management will give 2027 guidance on the fourth-quarter call (last year’s came on February 4), and CEO Rob Michael said on Friday’s call that he expects “top-tier growth again next year.” That forecast has to absorb the Medicare negotiated price for Vraylar, which starts in 2027. The dividend question is settled. A 52% adjusted payout falling toward 40% is not a strained dividend. The open question is the stock: at a 2.47% forward yield, holders are paying for that 15% EPS growth in 2027. If February’s guide lands near the Street’s $16.16, the price holds up. AbbVie just dropped its Q3 2026 report and the stock barely flinched, up about 1.4% to US$294.89 by the close. That is a muted move for a business that just printed US$17.4b in quarterly revenue and lifted full year adjusted earnings guidance to a midpoint of US$13.97 per share. The market is treating this like a routine beat, but the underlying message is louder. A richer net margin over the past year and a high 50.6x trailing P/E now collide with lingering worries about debt and negative equity. Love AbbVie’s rich margins and earnings guidance but uneasy about the leverage and negative equity overhang? Consider screening for drugmakers that pair healthy profitability with cleaner balance sheets in our list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals stocks (24 results) Earnings grab headlines, but investors who care about what AbbVie is actually worth usually spend more time on the cash flowing through the business. Those cash flows can tell a different story to reported profit in any single quarter. On AbbVie’s numbers, if you focus on cash generation rather than just this year’s big swing in earnings, the stock could be a dramatic 41% undervalued. AbbVie is often framed as a test of whether new drugs can truly replace Humira and Imbruvica. That ambition is laid out clearly. Immunology revenue of about US$34.9b for 2026, led by Skyrizi at US$21.8b and Rinvoq at US$11.2b, now meaningfully exceeds Humira’s shrinking US$683m quarterly haul. Neuroscience at roughly US$3.4b with fast growing Parkinson’s and migraine products adds further proof that replacement is happening, not just promised. On the flip side, concerns focus on whether competition and regulation will chip away at AbbVie’s newer pillars. Oncology revenue of about US$1.7b grew only 0.9% operationally as Imbruvica declined 26.1%. Gains from Venclexta, Epkinly and Elahere largely just patch the hole. That sluggish segment outcome, despite strong immunology and neuroscience, shows competitive and pricing headwinds are already visible rather than theoretical.
